title: Kingdom of the Isles
capsule: The Kingdom of the Isles (Innse Gall in Scottish Gaelic) encompassed the Hebrides and the Isle of Man under Norse-Gaelic lords who acknowledged nominal Norwegian suzerainty, emerging from Viking settlement of the Western Isles from the 9th century onward. Godred Crovan conquered Man in 1079 and welded the Hebrides into a single dynastic realm ruled from Man, his line dominating the seaways of the Irish Sea and the Minch. The unity he forged proved fragile: around 1156 Somerled, lord of Argyll, wrested the southern Hebrides away, permanently splitting the kingdom between his descendants and the Crovan dynasty of Man and the Northern Isles.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The island geography of the kingdom is fixed, but the extent of mainland territories under its control at different periods varied considerably and is imperfectly documented in Scottish and Norse sources.
